sentence: This project oversees the quality of knee images and the data taken from them to help study how joint structures relate to joint pain.
This project looks for drug targets within cellular signaling pathways to treat human disease.
This project holds an annual conference that brings together geneticists who study mammals to plan research and improve human health.
This project studies whether psilocybin can help the brain reduce fear and gain control over intrusive memories in post-traumatic stress disorder.
This project builds a technology that can show single cancer cells in tissue and during surgery.
This project tests whether two treatments given one after the other help T cells and B cells tolerate the body's own antigens.
This project builds a screening tool that finds enzymes making isoprenoids, which take part in cholesterol biosynthesis.
This project studies whether opsins act as bitter taste receptors in mosquitoes and in mammals.
This project uses genetics to find the human pathways that make and control nuclear long non-coding RNAs.
This project uses metabolic imaging with hyperpolarized carbon-13 to study glioblastoma and meningioma and how they respond to treatment.
This project studies how Endothelin-1 signaling controls adult neural stem cells during demyelination and remyelination.
This project supplies cell lines and organoids from humans and mice to study digestive and liver diseases.
This project builds a framework that uses real-world data to test how glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists affect mental health.
This project studies whether targeting transcriptional initiation and elongation helps treat diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, alone and with radiation.
This project looks for molecular and neuropathological signatures in Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal lobar degeneration and Long COVID.
This project studies how a vertebral stem cell controls bone formation in the spine.
This project uses in silico and in vivo methods to find genetic dependencies in subtypes of hepatocellular carcinoma.
This project studies how two checkpoint receptors work in adaptive and innate immunity against cancer.
This project builds computational methods based on population genetics to study how disease spread shapes the genetic diversity of pathogens.
This project manages and analyzes clinical, imaging and biomarker data collected across several research projects.
